title: Sentinel: Autonomous Monitoring
content:
Sentinel is Crystal Ball's autonomous monitoring system. It runs on a schedule, collects snapshots of all intelligence domains, evaluates alert rules, checks watchlists, and builds a historical record for trend analysis.

What sentinel does: On each cycle, sentinel queries all sidecar endpoints, saves a timestamped snapshot to disk, evaluates all active alert rules against current data, checks all watchlists for new activity, and optionally forwards triggered alerts to cb-control for push notifications.

History snapshots: Each sentinel run saves a JSON snapshot under sentinel/history/ with a timestamp-based filename. These snapshots form the baseline for trend() and anomaly_scan() — the more history you accumulate, the better the trend and anomaly analysis becomes. At least 2 snapshots are needed for trend analysis and 3 for anomaly detection.

Scheduling: Sentinel runs on a configurable interval. In normal mode, it polls at the default rate. In Ghost Mode, polling frequency increases by 5x while analytics and notifications are suppressed.

Alert evaluation: During each cycle, sentinel runs the equivalent of alert_check({}) and watchlist_check({}). Any triggered alerts or watchlist hits are included in the sentinel report.

Integration with cb-control: When cb-control is running, sentinel can forward triggered alerts as push notifications to iOS devices. This enables real-time monitoring without keeping a terminal open.

Best practices: Let sentinel run continuously to build up history. Set meaningful alert rules before enabling sentinel so you get actionable notifications. Review sentinel history periodically with trend() to spot gradual changes that individual snapshots might miss.
